page: Amazon Web Services m8a.4xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by the Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Geekbench testing also places its single-core and multi-core scores, image processing, and text processing in the top tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, static web serving throughput, and PassMark memory scores are rated as strong. However, multi-core stress-ng performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations fall into the average category.

The instance offers a balanced resource profile with high-speed DDR5 memory and strong single-core CPU capabilities, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be handled via network-attached options, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads.
This instance is suitable for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, text and image processing, software compilation, and small-scale language model inference.
